claims.text: The starting material is a conventionally sintered W–Cu composite with discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The starting composite exhibits phase separation and interfacial voids.
Post-sintering HIP will enhance bonding at W–Cu interfaces.
The proposed HIP treatment uses high temperature and high pressure for a brief duration under an inert atmosphere.
Pressure-assisted diffusion during HIP will reduce porosity at W–Cu interfaces.
HIP will drive localized interdiffusion across W/Cu boundaries.
Localized interdiffusion and applied pressure will heal pre-existing interfacial voids.
HIP will mitigate phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
Reduced interfacial defects will improve mechanical contact between W and Cu.
Improved interfacial contact will form more continuous thermal-conduction pathways.
HIP-treated W–Cu will have statistically significantly higher effective thermal conductivity than untreated W–Cu.
The thermal-conductivity advantage will remain under comparable cyclic heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
Interfacial voids and phase separation in untreated W–Cu compromise thermal conduction.
The approach is applicable to conventionally sintered W–Cu composites.
HIP parameters can be optimized to avoid excessive grain growth or unwanted phase transformations.
The applicable service envelope is the high-heat-flux and irradiation environment of joints between W plasma-facing components and Cu-based cooling components.
